title: Quantifying Node Importance over Network Structural Stability

problem.claim: Quantifying node importance based on its effects on engagement dynamics is important for supporting network stability.

gap.claim: Existing studies primarily use node coreness to estimate engagement importance from network topology.

contributions.claim: Defines node importance as the effect of strengthening or weakening a node's engagement on the engagement of other nodes.
Introduces anchor power for measuring overall coreness gain from node strengthening and collapse power for measuring overall coreness loss from node weakening.
Provides a shell component-based framework with a unified static algorithm for computing anchored and collapsed followers, plus maintenance techniques for evolving networks.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper explicitly presents anchor power and collapse power as two novel concepts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The evolving-network maintenance techniques are reported to be around three orders of magnitude faster than rerunning the static algorithm.
Experiments on real-life data are reported to demonstrate the effectiveness of the model and the efficiency of the algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper motivates node-importance quantification as a means to support network stability and user engagement.
Prior studies use node coreness as a standard topology-based estimate of engagement importance.
The paper defines importance through the effects of strengthening or weakening a node's engagement on other nodes.
It operationalizes this definition with anchor power and collapse power, then develops static and evolving-network algorithms.
Real-life experiments are reported as showing model effectiveness and algorithmic efficiency.

source_observation.claim: Node importance is measured through the network-wide coreness effects of strengthening or weakening a node.

interpretation.claim: Importance can be modeled as a structural stability response rather than only as a static node property.

application.claim: For engagement or retention interventions, evaluate both positive strengthening effects and negative weakening effects on network structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that coreness-based effects are sufficient for networks or objectives outside the described setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the real-life datasets, experimental metrics, or baselines.
The abstract does not provide the conditions underlying the reported three-orders-of-magnitude speedup.
The abstract does not describe reproducibility details or implementation availability.
